requirement_results.command: assembling context twice from identical pinned item versions, ordering, redaction, truncation and representation reproduces byte-identical receipt digests and ordered item references
bumping a single pinned item's version (content unchanged) changes the receipt digest
changing the redaction field set changes the receipt digest
a different query vector produces a genuinely different real Qdrant similarity ranking (verified by the first ordered item reference itself) and a different receipt digest
a tighter truncation budget changes the receipt digest and sets the truncated flag, versus an untruncated assembly which does not
changing only the representation version (identical items, ordering, redaction, truncation) changes the receipt digest even though the ordered item references are unchanged
two independent assemblies of the identical pinned inputs are observationally equivalent on both the digest and ordering axes, proven via the sealed cross-task equivalence helper
a real TCP connection refusal from a genuinely closed local port during ranking raises ContextReplayError rather than returning a silent partial or reordered context
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: The unreachable-ranking-backend fault-injection test uses a real OS-level TCP connection refusal (a QdrantHarness pointed at a genuinely closed local port) rather than pausing the shared self-provisioned container, consistent with OCOR-DEV-0026's established lower-blast-radius pattern; the refusal is a genuine network-layer fault, not a mocked exception.

ContextReceipt deliberately never re-exposes assembled content, only item_id@version references and the digest -- redaction and truncation are proven by digest divergence between otherwise-identical runs, not by inspecting the assembled text, since a receipt re-exposing redacted content would itself be a confidentiality leak.

Ordering is exercised against a real Qdrant similarity search (OCOR-DEV-0023's sealed QdrantHarness), not a synthetic sort -- the ordering-change test verifies a genuine change in the real backend's ranked output, not just a hand-constructed reordering.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test operates on a freshly self-provisioned Qdrant collection (a unique name per test run) torn down in a finally block regardless of outcome, so no test leaves residual state another run could collide with. Verified directly by 4 consecutive full test-suite runs with no manual cleanup between them, and by the post-run stack-integrity check confirming all 11 persistent services remained healthy.
